thread:
laura: Heads up — we just published the Private/VPC on-prem SLA fallback runbook and the formal incident-to-credit policy. Read it before next week's customer sync.

sandeep: Where's the link? also, quick TL;DR on how credits are calculated?

laura: Link (internal only): https://internal.redwood/team/private/sla-fallback-runbook

laura: TL;DR — If a customer's p95 latency breaches the configured SLO for a sustained window (10m) and Redwood confirms the degradation is due to allocation/fallback behavior (not customer app code), we will: 1) attempt an automated fallback to a compatible model variant, 2) trigger a 30m temporary capacity burst if spare capacity exists, 3) if service is still degraded, apply a pro-rata SLA credit per the contract.

laura: Credit formula: prorated_hours_degraded * monthly_committed_fee / total_hours_in_billing_month. Ops and finance folks check my math :)

ryan_pm: Is this retroactive to current Private customers or only for new addenda?

laura: Applies to customers with an SLA addendum signed after 2025-01-01. For legacy contracts we'll offer the fallback/runbook support operationally, but credit terms require an amendment — Legal will follow up if the customer opts in.

maria_security: Important security note: to validate incidents for credits we require telemetry + audit logs enabled. If telemetry is disabled by the customer, we can do diagnostics, but any credits will be manually reviewed and may take longer to approve. Add this to onboarding.

jess: Noted. I'll add a telemetry opt-in checkbox to the onboarding checklist and schedule a 30m training for CS/SEs next Tue to walk through the runbook.

caleb: Ops q: what's the alert rule? Can we reuse a Prometheus example? e.g.:

caleb: ```yaml
- alert: PrivateOnPrem_P95LatencyHigh
  expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))) > 1.2
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Private instance P95 latency above SLO"
```

laura: Perfect — that's the sample we'll publish. Runbook also includes a safe fallback CLI for on-call: 

laura: ```bash
redwood private fallback --site $SITE_ID --model rdx-compat-small --reason "sla_fallback"
```

engbot: Note: policy doc and runbook pushed to /team/private at 16:00 UTC. Version v1.0.

ops-bot: Runbook tag created: private-sla-fallback, runbook-id: rb-2026-042.

sandeep: Does runtime need to change anything for auto-fallback? Router + model variant registry touched?

laura: Yes — runtime must enforce a compatibility guard: only fallback to variants marked compatible with the original model (tokenization and response schema must match). Product will publish a compatibility checklist by EOD.

ryan_pm: I'll file a cross-team playbook task. CS will draft a customer-facing note by Friday.

maria_security: Reminder: exercising burst capacity into a customer's VPC requires cross-team approval and ephemeral creds. Ops Sec will circulate the approval flow and an approval template.

jess: RSVP to the training if you're in Private onboarding or SRE support. Agenda: policy overview, runbook walkthrough, demo of fallback CLI, Q&A.

laura: If you have customers to proactively offer the new SLA addendum to (high spend / regulated), ping me or @ryan_pm. Thanks everyone.
